name: Park MGM Las Vegas
positioning: Smoke-free resort on the Las Vegas Strip, steps from T-Mobile Arena, with a French garden-style pool deck, sage green and brass design, and the Dolby Live theater
best_for: Travelers who want a smoke-free Strip base close to T-Mobile Arena and Dolby Live shows
Guests who prefer design-led rooms and a pool deck with three pools and private cabanas

facts.text: Park MGM Las Vegas is steps away from T-Mobile Arena and the Park outdoor entertainment space.
Park MGM Las Vegas is a smoke-free resort.
The hotel is set just south of the center of the Las Vegas Strip.
Guests can unwind at one of three pools or in a private cabana.
The public spaces have a slight French look, with marble floors, sage green trim work and brass detailing.
Park MGM was previously the Monte Carlo resort.
The property's transformation, completed in 2018, was a partnership between MGM Resorts International and Sydell Group.
Room decor comes in one of two palettes: the hotel's signature sage green or a bright red.
The Nighthawk Suite is the hotel's corner suite.
The Park MGM Two Queen room offers two queen beds and an open floor plan.
The Library is a book-lined space.

highlights.text: The three pools sit on a French garden-style pool deck.
The lobby is anchored by a tree-like sculpture hanging from the ceiling in place of a crystal chandelier.
The Dolby Live theater, formerly the Park Theater, has hosted residencies including Lady Gaga, Cher and Aerosmith.
On the Record is a speakeasy-meets-nightclub set behind an actual record store.
Instead of typical hotel art, rooms have gallery walls curated by Le Studio be-poles.

considerations.text: The spa and salon are rather small, though they have locker rooms with hot tubs, steam rooms and saunas.
The rooms do not have a bathtub.
WhataHotel notes that resort fees and parking charges apply.
